    • There’s… a lot… of coverage surrounding the revamped Chase Sapphire Reserve Card.
    • Recent findings suggest that the changes really fit my profile and sure, the card will cost more, but I won’t have to introduce any behavior change to get more, unlike some other cards.
    • Well, if my first Chase Sapphire Reserve redemption is any indicator, this card may single handedly change the redemption game and just about everyone should take note — including airline and hotel transfer partners.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There’s… a lot… of coverage surrounding the revamped Chase Sapphire Reserve Card. As per usual these days, the hot takes are plentiful and people are fired up. It’s either the apocalypse or the beginning of something great, depending on which attention seeker you read. As a long time cardholder, I’m really intrigued by the newly introduced changes.

    Recent findings suggest that the changes really fit my profile and sure, the card will cost more, but I won’t have to introduce any behavior change to get more, unlike some other cards. I’ll do most of my spending on this card. I’m a keeper just from the fee credit and earning multipliers.

    But what about the redemption of points?

    Well, if my first Chase Sapphire Reserve redemption is any indicator, this card may single handedly change the redemption game and just about everyone should take note — including airline and hotel transfer partners. It’s already a huge win.

    It has been revealed that chase Travel’s ‘The Edit’ is a curated selection of nice hotels, which offer benefits similar to those provided by a travel agent or other luxury credit card booking platform. When booking a ‘The Edit’ property, you can expect breakfast for two, a $100 F&B credit, late check out and an upgrade subject to availability.

    Sources indicate that which leads me to the important bit! With the revamped Sapphire Reserve Card, there’s a fresh “Points Boost” feature, which offers up to two cents per point (25,000 points would cover $500, etc) for some flight or hotel purchases.

    This can be amazing value, with flights of $3,000 being grabbed for just 150,000 points, with no taxes and fees and the ability to still earn frequent flyer miles and elite status points, since the airline treats it like a cash ticket.

    Previously, the Sapphire Reserve card offered a steady point redemption opportunity directly on Chase Travel at 1.5 cents per point (100,000 points would cover $1500, etc). But with the fresh version, some travel purchases you want to redeem for will either offer less value than before, the same, or more, with this new ‘Points Boost’ at 2 cents per point. We like more!

    It has been revealed that I am in New York and wanted to do a little staycation, so I fired up Chase Travel and found one of my more reliable upper mid-scale hotels, The Thompson Central Park was on as part of ‘The Edit’. My two options became a very clear singular, third option.

    Typically, I’d consider paying cash or transferring my points from Chase to Hyatt to pay for a stay like this. Hyatt has “fixed” points rates, meaning the points price is largely irrespective of the cash price and only changes by seasonal dates. For this season, it was 25,000 points per night for the Thompson Central Park.

    If I were to transfer my points, I’d get a free night (the cash rate was around $500) and have a really solid points redemption at exactly two cents per point. I’m not loyal to any hotel chain really, so I wouldn’t get any breakfast or “elite” benefits, but a free night is a free night.

    BUT — Chase Travel had a ‘Points Boost’ option to book the hotel directly on their platform and not transfer points to Hyatt. Chase Travel was offering this property for circa 25,000 points and that would cover the $500 cash rate, but unlike transferring points to Hyatt, because I was redeeming a ‘The Edit’ property on Chase Travel, I’d receive….

    It has been revealed that yep, by NOT transferring my points (and dealing with the fractured transfer journey) I was able to get myself basically $200 in additional value added to my stay with the breakfast and $100 property credit, not factoring in the value of late check out or a category room upgrade. In addition, I’ll be able to earn elite nights and Hyatt Points on the stay.

    According to recent reports, A mere 25,000 Chase Ultimate Rewards Points got me a “free” $500 hotel night, breakfast for two, and $100 to spend at the hotel. That’s a pretty stunning redemption, giving more than two cents per point of value and still allowing me to earn on the stay, unlike when you transfer your points to a loyalty program. I wish I could’ve stayed longer.

    For the first time I can remember, transferring points to Hyatt was not the best option here and that’s something to stand up and take notice of.

    If Chase can keep up this Points Boost game, it can really send ripples through rewards. For the first time, people can easily receive tremendous value for their points through a credit card portal while still earning elite status and points with the hotel or airline of their choosing.

    You can check out the newly introduced 100,000 point + 500 travel credit offer for the Sapphire Reserve. It’s 200,000 points for Sapphire Reserve Business Cards.

    Are US Flight Schedules Returning to Normal? What Thanksgiving Travelers Need to Know

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1220 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Travel chaos erupted at US airports over the weekend following a historic FAA ground stop that paused all flight takeoffs across the country for nearly five hours.
    • The ground stop, declared by the FAA amid air traffic control complications on Friday, November 13, stranded millions of fliers nationwide, with tens of thousands of flight delays and cancellations continuing for days.
    • In a recent development, fortunately for travelers, both federal officials and airlines are doing everything they can to get flight schedules back on track and have airport operations running smoothly in time for the holiday rush.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Travel chaos erupted at US airports over the weekend following a historic FAA ground stop that paused all flight takeoffs across the country for nearly five hours.

    The ground stop, declared by the FAA amid air traffic control complications on Friday, November 13, stranded millions of fliers nationwide, with tens of thousands of flight delays and cancellations continuing for days. Now, with the busy Thanksgiving travel period fast approaching, travelers are wondering when US air travel system will return to normal.

    In a recent development, fortunately for travelers, both federal officials and airlines are doing everything they can to get flight schedules back on track and have airport operations running smoothly in time for the holiday rush. “Recovery to normal operations will be slow and steady,” says a November 15 statement from the FAA. “We ask for your patience as airlines work to get you to your destination.”.

    Although the incident is frustrating, experts say that travelers shouldn’t be concerned about the safety of the air traffic control system. “While the disruption was significant, travelers should take confidence in knowing that safety remained the top priority throughout the incident,” notes Geoff Freeman, president and CEO of the US Travel Association. “Our aviation professionals deserve tremendous credit for managing the crisis and getting Americans safely back on their way.".

    If you have Thanksgiving travel plans and you're flying out this week, here's what to know about the current state of air travel in the US.

    Recent findings suggest that the ground stop was issued due to air traffic control equipment outages and complications with telecommunications systems that the FAA uses to track and communicate with planes while they’re flying. “The ground stop was issued out of an abundance of caution,” states the FAA’s statement. “Safety is, and will always remain, the FAA’s highest priority. We will never compromise the safety of the flying public.”.

    In a recent development, on Friday afternoon, the FAA’s network service provider, L3Harris, was updating telecommunications equipment at an FAA facility in El Dorado, Arkansas, when the problems began, according to the FAA. The organization was deploying a fresh router that also began to cause system disruptions at a radar site in Amarillo, Texas. “The FAA’s legacy equipment became unstable when data began flooding the FAA FTI network, at a rate of 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds,” states an FAA statement. “This disrupted the system and created instability with aircraft communications and radar feeds.”.

    Once the inconsistencies were identified, the FAA claims that L3Harris blocked those two locations, and the network stabilized. However, the exact cause of the telecommunications issues are still under investigation.

    Industry observers note that regulators are still working to identify the root cause of the concern. “The work that was done on Friday, that's been done thousands of times by L3Harris in our network,” Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy noted in a Sunday interview on ABC’s “This Week.” “It's been done thousands of times by other companies, and these issues haven't arisen, and so that's why we have to figure out what went wrong here.”.

    Duffy also noted that the equipment in question is several decades old: the router was originally purchased in 2001 and was also part of a system that ran on obsolete copper wiring.

    It has been revealed that experts say that the archaic equipment underscores the urgent need to update the nation’s air traffic control system. “While the investigation continues, the incident exposed a troubling reality: America's aviation system remains vulnerable because we have relied on aging infrastructure for far too long,” notes Freeman. “Friday's disruption was a wake-up call that Washington cannot afford to ignore.”.

    Air travel experts say that the ground stop’s effects on Thanksgiving travel plans beginning later this week should be minimal.

    As of Monday afternoon, the majority of airline flight schedules were back on track. There were still about 2,800 flight delays within, into, or out of the US on Monday, and nearly 330 flight cancellations, according to FlightAware data. It also helps that fewer travelers are expected to fly this year compared to recent years. According to Mike Arnot, spokesman for Cirium, an aviation analytics company, the Wednesday before Thanksgiving is usually the busiest air travel day of the year. But in 2026, it’s not even slated to be in the top 50 busiest days for flying,.

    Sources indicate that american Airlines, the largest carrier at DFW, said its operations were returning to normal on Monday. “American is prepared to operate a largely normal schedule Monday, Nov. 16, following the FAA's nationwide ground stop,” the carrier said in a statement. "With crews and aircraft in position and favorable weather expected across our system, we are set up for a good start to the week and do not anticipate additional broad cancellations related to this incredibly disruptive industry-wide event.”.

    In a recent development, delta has also advised its passengers traveling on Monday to continue to allow extra time at the airport for any lingering effects on flight schedules. “While most flights are operating normally, some customers may still experience delays or cancellations,” the carrier said.

    Travelers should still continue to check with their airline for the latest travel updates and blueprint to be at the airport at least two hours before takeoff for a domestic flight.

    Operations are largely back on track, so many airlines have ended the flexible rebooking waivers that were issued at the beginning of the ground stop. However, two major carriers still have travel waivers in place.

    Delta is still allowing passengers scheduled to fly through Monday, November 16, to make changes to their flights at no extra cost through November 23. Travelers’ new departure dates must be on or before November 23, according to the airline’s rebooking policy.

    American Airlines is waiving change fees for passengers booked to travel to or from one of 21 major US airports through Wednesday, November 18. Passengers can choose a latest travel date through November 21, but all changes must be made by November 18.

    According to recent reports, even if your airline no longer has a travel waiver in place, if you’re flying with a major US carrier, you likely have the ability to change your flight without paying a fee (although a difference in fare may apply). However, these policies usually do not apply to low-cost carriers or tickets booked in basic economy class.

    Sources indicate that it’s impossible to predict if a nationwide ground stop could happen again, according to Freeman. However, modernizing the air traffic control system should reduce these types of outages over the long run.

    Sources indicate that “The FAA is making progress, replacing outdated copper communications lines with high-speed fiber, upgrading radar and radio systems, and introducing technology that allows air traffic controllers to manage flights more efficiently,” Freeman says. “For travelers, these investments should mean fewer delays, more reliable flights, and greater confidence that the system can handle disruptions.”.

    In a recent development, airline executives echoed a similar sentiment regarding the state of US air traffic control systems. “This moment must be a call to action,” United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby said in a statement emailed to media. “It is critical for safety, our passengers, and our economy that we fix our nation’s Air Traffic Control system now.”.

    • United mentioned it has resolved a system outage that delayed flights across its network late Monday afternoon.
    • “We have resolved a technology glitch that delayed flight departures,” the airline mentioned in a statement.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    United mentioned it has resolved a system outage that delayed flights across its network late Monday afternoon.

    “We have resolved a technology glitch that delayed flight departures,” the airline mentioned in a statement. “While some flights were delayed, there was no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights. There is no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue.”.

    Between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m. Eastern time, crews at multiple airports reported they could not get the final weight-and-balance figures required for departure.

    It has been revealed that united acknowledged a “widespread system outage” in a post on X. In a separate statement, the carrier remarked it was “troubleshooting a technology issue affecting departing flights.”.

    According to recent reports, the first report identified in radio audio captured by the ATC App came at about 4:02 p.m. ET, when the crew of United flight 2787 in Denver reported trouble getting its final weights. At Chicago O’Hare, the system used to request pushbacks also went down. At Newark, a ramp controller said the outage affected how ramp crews received gate changes.

    “We are having an extreme system-wide outage… which is preventing us from closing out flights, which is affecting pretty much all of our mainline departures at this point,” an O’Hare ramp controller mentioned.

    Recent findings suggest that radio reports named at least 30 United flights across 12 airports. Some crews at O’Hare and Los Angeles reported receiving final weights between 4:40 and 5:09 p.m. ET. At 5:11 p.m., an O’Hare ramp controller canceled a United flight’s pushback after it had waited about 20 minutes.

    Republicans tap Moreno and Jack to lead Senate and House campaign arms

    📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (666 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that house and Senate Republicans picked their newly introduced campaign chiefs Tuesday, tasking Ohio Sen.
    • In their fresh positions, both will spearhead Republicans’ push to win back majorities on Capitol Hill after Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress by flipping more than 40 House seats and at least seven Senate seats in last week’s midterm elections.
    • Republicans returned to Capitol Hill this week still reeling from their losses but resisted calls to delay Tuesday’s leadership elections.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that house and Senate Republicans picked their newly introduced campaign chiefs Tuesday, tasking Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno and Georgia Rep. Brian Jack with leading the GOP campaign arms for the 2028 election cycle.

    In their fresh positions, both will spearhead Republicans’ push to win back majorities on Capitol Hill after Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress by flipping more than 40 House seats and at least seven Senate seats in last week’s midterm elections.

    Republicans returned to Capitol Hill this week still reeling from their losses but resisted calls to delay Tuesday’s leadership elections. In the Senate, South Dakota’s John Thune was reelected Republican leader without any opposition, while Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan defeated Louisiana Rep. Steve Scalise in a closed-door, secret-ballot election to lead House Republicans next year.

    In a recent development, moreno will succeed South Carolina Sen. Tim Scott as chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee.

    “Republicans must enter this next election clear-eyed: the road ahead back to a Republican Senate majority will by no means be easy but the fight has never been so important,” the Ohio senator stated in a statement.

    Speaking to reporters on Capitol Hill, Moreno described his latest role as “a hell of a job.” He said Republicans would be “absolute savages” on ending government corruption and continuing “to work for the American people.”.

    “I suspect the best tailwind we’ll have is that the Democrats will learn all the wrong lessons,” he told reporters.

    It has been revealed that moreno, a close ally of President Donald Trump, is currently serving his first term. He first ran for Senate during the 2022 cycle but dropped out of a crowded GOP primary eventually won by JD Vance. Two years later, buoyed by an endorsement from Trump, he won a contested primary for the state’s other Senate seat and went on to oust Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown that fall.

    Industry observers note that brown is poised to return to the Senate after defeating appointed Republican Sen. Jon Husted last week in a special election for the remaining Senate term of Vice President Vance. While Ohio has swung heavily toward Republicans over the past decade, Democrats scored big wins in the Buckeye State last week, winning several statewide offices and flipping three seats in the U.S. House.

    But assuming he runs again for a full term, Brown will be on the ballot in 2028, setting up what’s likely to be a tense home-state fight.

    Industry observers note that in an apparent reference to the returning Brown, Moreno offered some Washington advice Tuesday: “Make sure you rent. Do not buy.”.

    The 2028 Senate map gives Republican pickup opportunities in a handful of swing states, including Arizona, Georgia, Nevada, Newly introduced Hampshire and Pennsylvania. The party will also be defending battleground seats in Alaska, Iowa, North Carolina and Wisconsin. Also on the Senate ballot are races for Republican-held seats in Kansas and South Carolina, where Democrats scored surprise wins last week.

    On the House side, Jack defeated Indiana Rep. Rudy Yakym III to become the next chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee. He takes office after one of the worst elections for the GOP in recent decades and will succeed outgoing NRCC Chair Richard Hudson, who lost his own North Carolina seat last week.

    It has been revealed that house Republicans face the tough task of cutting into Democrats’ 40-plus-seat majority next cycle. But the party will have a slew of pickup opportunities, given the sheer number of seats Democrats won in historically red territory this year.

    In a recent development, like Moreno, Jack was first elected to Congress 2024, leveraging a close relationship with Trump to win an open seat outside Atlanta. He previously was White House director of political affairs during Trump’s first term and was a senior adviser to the president’s 2024 campaign. Over the past two years, he served as the NRCC’s recruitment chair.

    Savannah Behrmann contributed to this report.

    #30638. Latest Update: Review: Park Hyatt Vienna, My Favorite Hotel In The Austrian Capital

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2583 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Liveandletsfly ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Review: Park Hyatt Vienna, My Favorite Hotel In The Austrian Capital

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2583 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the Park Hyatt Vienna is not only my favorite hotels in Vienna, but one of my favorite Hyatt properties in the world.
    • Although we could have connected directly to Zürich after landing in Vienna, I was able to force a 23.5-hour layover into the itinerary, which gave us a chance to stay to the Park Hyatt Vienna, a hotel I’ve enjoyed many times over the years but it was the first time my children had come along.
    • I booked this for 35,000 World of Hyatt points (versus a cash rate of over €700) and applied a “Guest of Honor” to the reservation, which essentially marks me as “Globalist” in the system.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the Park Hyatt Vienna is not only my favorite hotels in Vienna, but one of my favorite Hyatt properties in the world. With excellent service, nice amenities, delicious breakfast, and central location, our latest stay was another great reminder of what a superb property this is.

    Although we could have connected directly to Zürich after landing in Vienna, I was able to force a 23.5-hour layover into the itinerary, which gave us a chance to stay to the Park Hyatt Vienna, a hotel I’ve enjoyed many times over the years but it was the first time my children had come along.

    I booked this for 35,000 World of Hyatt points (versus a cash rate of over €700) and applied a “Guest of Honor” to the reservation, which essentially marks me as “Globalist” in the system.

    Recent findings suggest that our Austrian flight landed at 11:30 am into VIE and I had emailed the hotel requesting an early check-in, specifically noting that we would be happy to forgo an upgrade in order to access our room a few hours early. Our request was honored.

    It has been revealed that the Park Hyatt Vienna is ideally located on Am Hof in the heart of the old town, an easy walk from St. Stephen’s Cathedral and many of the places I most enjoy visiting in Vienna.

    Checking in, I was welcomed back to the hotel and the amenities were explained, including breakfast and pool hours (most vital to my kids!).

    Industry observers note that we were assigned room 331, a standard room with two twins beds. While not an upgrade, the room was spacious enough and quite comfortable with a desk, round table, chair, and the two beds.

    My daughter jumped right into bed to go to sleep (it was, after all, about 3:15 am in Los Angeles), but I pulled her out: no napping today would hopefully mean no jet lag tomorrow.

    The bathroom featured really beautiful stonework behind the bathtub and included two sinks, a separate water closet, and walk-in shower.

    The room had a wardrobe that included a coffee machine, hot water kettle, and mini-bar including snacks and drinks.

    A welcome amenity was also waiting for us including various chocolates and candies.

    Recent findings suggest that the room had plenty of 220-volt outlets and also a safe to lock valuables. Unfortunately, the room did not have any USB-C ports or wireless chargers.

    A primary reason I booked this hotel was for the pool and wellness. My kids love to swim and I can’t think of a better hotel pool than this one: we spent a lot of time here in the afternoon and evening.

    The entire pool and spa area is posh, with a full-range of treatments available but nice say chairs with fresh peaches and plums, a locker room, and a wellness area with a sauna and steam room available to all guests.

    Side note: the hotel has a cryogenic machine in the spa that will let you stand in -110ºC temperatures for three minutes…I was tempted and probably would have tried it had I been alone.

    Thankfully, there was no drama this time in the sauna!

    > Read More: Accused Of Being A Child Predator at Park Hyatt Vienna!

    According to recent reports, the fitness center is located in the spa area on the lower level, but accessible 24/7 with your room card and includes TechnoGym equipment. I awoke an hour before the kids and went down to workout…a nice way to start the day and fight jet lag.

    You mustn’t skip breakfast here, for it is truly a treat.

    The Bank is the most beautiful part of the hotel: an ornate dining room that was once the grand lobby when this hotel was still a bank. Breakfast is served from 7:00 am each morning until 10:30 am (11:00 am on weekends) and includes a delicious buffet plus an additional a la carte menu. If breakfast isn’t clouded in your rate, it is €58 each, which while steep is really worthwhile considering all you get with it.

    There’s a bar section in The Bank that includes alcohol, including a large cocktail menu, and lighter food. It’s open from 9:00 am to 1:00 am on Monday – Wednesday, till 2:00 am on Thursday – Saturday, and from 5:00 pm to 1:00 pm on Sunday (good luck finding anything open on Sunday in Vienna…).

    The hotel’s Viennese café includes cakes, coffee and chocolates, as well as alcoholic drinks and snacks, with an outdoor terrace. Open each day from 9:00 am to 8:00 pm.

    It has been revealed that open from 9:00 am to 6:00 pm daily, the Lounge offers a more informal dining experience where you can enjoy hot and cold drinks plus a variety of food. Menu here.

    According to recent reports, finally, 24/7 room service is available. Menu here.

    There used to be really posh cigar lounge in this hotel, but now it is a beauty salon (Vienna has banned indoor smoking after being a smoker’s haven for so many years).

    Our entire say was marked by one pleasant service encounter after another. I had a nice extended conversation with teh doorman and another great conversation with the agent who checked me in. We had a nice chat with our waitress in The Bank and the spa staff was also very friendly. I do speak German, albeit with an American accent, and appreciated that the staff was willing to engage in my less-than-perfect German as opposed to switching to English.

    This was another wonderful stay at the Park Hyatt Vienna and I’ll sum it up by saying simply that I cannot wait to return.

    In a recent development, my original review is below, dating all the way back to August 2014. Heidi and I went for my birthday just weeks after we got married…the hotel had recently opened and we had a great stay. It’s nice to see this hotel age so gracefully and what a joy it is to share this property and the lovely city of Vienna with my children.

    Industry observers note that vienna is a stately city rich with majestic architecture, an erudite culture, and a regal sense of style. In the center of the old city, replete with cobblestone walkways, horse drawn carriages, and glistening statues of historical luminaries, a new Park Hyatt hotel has opened on the site of a former monarchical bank. My wife and I celebrated my birthday in Vienna last weekend and stayed for two nights at Park Hyatt’s newest property.

    According to recent reports, A historic property located on Am Hof 2 in the heart of the First District of Vienna, a UNESCO World Heritage site, the hotel’s location cannot be beat. Within a few paces is the Goldenes Quartier shopping district, St. Stephan’s Cathedral, Hofburg Palace, Spanish Riding School, and many museums.

    Recent findings suggest that we began the day in Frankfurt with an early flight on Austrian Airlines to Vienna. I sent a note to the main hotel e-mail, park.vienna@hyatt.com, just before takeoff requesting an early check-in and had a response waiting when I landed in Vienna – the room was ready.

    In a recent development, from Vienna Airport you have two public transportation options for getting into the city – the City Airport Train (CAT) which travels non-stop to the heart of Vienna or a suburban train (S-Bahn) which calls at several stations on the way into town, taking about 15 minutes longer than the direct service. The CAT is 14EUR one-way while the S-Bahn is 4.40EUR. We took the S-Bahn into town, then connected on the underground train (U-Bahn) to Herrengasse Station, which is just a short walk from the hotel.

    In a recent development, A smiling porter greeted us outside the door and took our luggage. Inside, a friendly young man checked us in, speaking first in English when he noticed my American passport but then switching to German upon the request of my wife that I practice my Deutsch! He escorted us upstairs and demonstrated the hi-tech features of our room. Like many Park Hyatt properties, lighting and draperies are electronically controlled by a central push-button unit.

    I loved the room – a spacious standard room with tremendous natural light, a great view, and functionality. The room featured copious electrical outlets – an essential amenity when taking my business on the road, as I did here even on my birthday weekend. The layout of the couch in front of the bed in front of the desk nicely utilized the space in the room and the separate entry hall insulated the room from outside noise.

    Two doors decorated in geometric art-deco style, closed off the bathroom and entry hall from the bedroom. The bathroom was very large (and well-placed mirrors made it appear even larger) and featured a sizeable bathtub, walk-in rain shower, two sinks, and a separate water closet.

    According to recent reports, A minibar featured an Illy coffee machine with several packets of complimentary espresso and snack and drink for purchase. The refrigerator did make a rather loud humming sound that could be heard even when the bedroom door was closed. I am a heavy sleeper, but my wife woke me up one night to “turn the climate off” yet it was not the air conditioning, it was the refrigerator! It was not terrible, just noticeable.

    It was warm outside and we had a problem getting the air conditioning to activate. Turns out one of the windows was open just ajar – just make sure all your windows are tightly shut and your room key is in the slot by the door or else your air conditioning will not function. Once on, the room cooled down rapidly. Vienna boasts exceptional weather so most of the year there is no need for a/c anyway.

    The hotel offers three dining options in addition to 24-hour room service; The Bank, Pearl, and The Lobby Lounge. Pearl bar features an outdoor terrace in addition to a contemporary indoor seating area and specializes in cocktails. A tapas menu is available with food as substantial as Wiener Schnitzel also available.

    It has been revealed that the Lobby Lounge offers drinks and light meals and sits next to the Living Room, a cigar and whiskey lounge that is one of the hotel’s best features. Admittedly, I see little value in setting fire to and then inhaling a plant that is linked to lung cancer but many of my friends and my brother hold a different opinion, so I find myself in cigar bars quite often. If you are a conneousier of cigars or just enjoy an opulent room to enjoy a drink in with friends, this bar is not to be missed. With plush couches and rich wooden paneling on the walls, I felt like I was part of the gentry mulling over world affairs in the cigar and brandy room onboard the Titanic.

    According to recent reports, finally, The Bank is the hotel’s most opulent restaurant and central to the character of the property. Here, on the site of the former cashier’s hall, we had breakfast each morning. Breakfast was 33EUR and the buffet was expansive with all that you would expect in a comprehensive breakfast—fresh squeezed juices, cereals, fruits, breads, cold-cuts, cheeses, breakfast meats, and eggs. Coffee (it was tremendous) as well as pancakes, waffles, French Toast, and eggs are included in the buffet and can be ordered from your server.

    We spent hours in here each morning enjoying a leisurely breakfast (breakfast ends at 10:30a during the week and 11:00a on weekends) and found the service to be warm, personal, and punctual. I thought everything was great – my wife had a problem with her eggs on the first morning (soft boiled eggs came out hard-boiled, then an omelet ordered with no cheese was delivered with cheese) but the concerns were promptly remedied and did not reoccur the next morning. The juices were remarkably tasty (apple, orange, and even grapefruit were exceptional) and my favorite part of the breakfast was the cheese-covered cooked tomatoes.

    Lunch and dinner are also offered each night in The Bank and you will find no menu posted online because the menu, sourced with local ingredients, changes often. Prices were moderate and I was prepared to dine at the restaurant for my birthday, but when mentioning that I was especially looking for fish, the concierge directed me to a restaurant called Kornat about 15 minutes away by foot, which specializes in fish and seafood.

    So I missed trying out The Bank for an evening meal, but I did appreciate the restaurant recommendation for the food was amazing and we enjoyed a prime outdoor table thanks to a call ahead from the concierge.

    I do have one gripe and only one true gripe about the property: the in-room wireless internet speed was unreliable. The Park Hyatt Vienna offers complimentary wired and wi-fi internet, which is a nice feature, but I found myself on multiple occasions banging my hand on the desk with disgust as poor connectivity led to unacceptably long page load times and the inability to make internet-based telephone calls. Other times, though, the interent worked perfectly well with pages loading fast and no matter with Skype calls or viewing YouTube videos. Admittedly, I did not not bring my ethernet cable converter for my MacBook Air so I was unable to test the wired internet speed.

    A large fitness studio with state-of-the-art, brand new equipment was much appreciated. Several bikes, treadmills, and ellipticals filled one side of the room while strength training equipment and free weights filled out the other. The room itself, with brass candelabras and wooden floors was an elegant place to work out and apples, bottled water, refrigerated towels, newspapers, and magazines were available.

    According to recent reports, the gym overlooks the swimming pool below, which sits on the site of the former bank vault. With an ornate frieze relief and elongated white leather couches, it offers a refreshing antidote to the hot afternoon sun (or cold). Adjacent to the pool is a lounge with chairs to relax and also steam room and sauna facilities. My one regret is that we did not spend an extra day in Vienna just to lounge around the spa. Certainly, seeing Vienna is the priority if your time is limited, but this is a great complimentary benefit of the hotel that seems to go unutilized, as I saw many hotel guests and no one using the pool or spa lounge. Full spa services are available here in the Arany Spa and you can even see the original 3-ton bank vault door.

    This hotel is a category six property, meaning it is 25,000 Hyatt Gold Passport points per night or 12,500 points plus a $150 co-pay (my preferred method of payment to help stretch out my points). The daily rate during the summer is about 375EUR or $500. Gold Passport availblity is good.

    I can’t tell you how much I enjoyed the city of Vienna and both my wife (who is not usually a city person) and I wish to return soon. When we do, we will definitely choose the Park Hyatt again, allowing an extra day for the spa and enjoying at a more leisurely pace one of Europe’s greatest capital cities.

    #30637. Well-Traveled Women on Where They Plan to Visit in 2027

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cntraveler ↗ Open Full Page

    Well-Traveled Women on Where They Plan to Visit in 2027

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1464 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that A bucket list item is one thing—turning it into an itinerary is another.
    • Sources indicate that with 2027 in sight, we’re taking inspiration from well-traveled women who are already thinking about the possibilities of the fresh, latest year ahead and the trips they hope to pull off.
    • Sources indicate that “For as long as I can remember, I’ve dreamed of diving in Antarctica.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that A bucket list item is one thing—turning it into an itinerary is another. The difference often lies in deciding that the places we dream about are worth pursuing amid limited vacation days and financial constraints. It’s a sentiment captured by avid traveler and content creator, Lucrenzia Worthington: “If there's one thing I've learned, it's that it’s never the right time, only the time you finally decide to go.”.

    Sources indicate that with 2027 in sight, we’re taking inspiration from well-traveled women who are already thinking about the possibilities of the fresh, latest year ahead and the trips they hope to pull off. Spanning photographers, artisans, interior designers, rock climbers, divers, and cookbook authors, they're wanderlust is as varied as it is far-reaching. Read on for how they plan to travel next, from diving Antarctica’s crystalline waters to cooking in the fertile valleys of the Peloponnese Peninsula.

    Sources indicate that “For as long as I can remember, I’ve dreamed of diving in Antarctica. Maybe it’s growing up in Bangkok’s tropical heat, but the polar regions endlessly fascinate me: the icebergs, the seals, and penguins. I’ve visited the White Continent before, but seeing it underwater is something else entirely. In 2027, I’m joining Aurora Expeditions, a pioneer in polar diving for over 20 years. Even as an experienced diver and underwater photographer, it takes serious preparation: I’m logging drysuit dives off [the coast of] Cape Town with specialized gear to get ready for one of the most extraordinary dive sites on earth.” —Pier Nirandara, travel writer, underwater photographer, and founder of Immersiv Expeditions.

    “You know, I've been lucky enough to see some extraordinary corners of the world, yet one place keeps slipping down my list. It's always ’not the right time,’ always ’too complicated to book.’ But 2027 is the year: Lapland, in February. There are direct flights from Milan to Rovaniemi, Finland, and I would initiative two nights there and two in Levi. I'm dreaming of a night in those super cool glass cabins where you fall asleep under the northern lights and endless starry skies, and booking experiences like visiting a reindeer farm, husky sledding, and snowshoe hikes through frosted pines—but also cozy up indoors by a crackling fire, with a warm blanket, and soak up the winter wonderland around me. If there's one thing I've learned, it's that it’s never the right time, only the time you finally decide to go.” —Lucrezia Worthington, content creator and freelance journalist.

    “I've always wanted to visit Morocco, and I think 2027 is the year. My dream is to stay in a riad in Marrakech with however many friends I can persuade to join me. I want to find tagine and wander through the [medina]. I also hope to venture out to the Atlas Mountains for a weekend.” —Ríoghnach Robinson, author of Bad Words.

    In a recent development, “In 2027, I'm planning to return to Antalya, Turkey. I spent a week there this year and fell in love with the food, the people, and the climbing. I'll be based around Geyikbayırı and Çitdibi, where there are limestone crags in the hills with views out to the sea. I usually find a place to stay on Airbnb and lean on local recommendations for where to eat. One spot I'm definitely returning to is Coffee Roaster 404.” —Sasha DiGiulian, professional climber and founder of SEND Bars.

    In a recent development, “Most flock to Greece for the idyllic beaches and all things Mediterranean, and while I completely understand that desire, my curiosity has landed me in the Peloponnese Peninsula, in particular the central region of Arcadia. Its fertile valleys are known for strong culinary and agricultural traditions; apples, sour cherries, slender eggplants, cheeses from mountain sheep and goats, walnuts, chestnuts, and mushroom foraging. I have been obsessing over a beautiful hotel that caught my eye: Manna, located on Mount Mainalo among hiking trails and dense forests. The mountain is also known for a very special high altitude honey cultivated from fir trees. Honestly, the honey alone is enough to get me on a plane.” —Noreen Wasti, cook, food creative, and author of Feast Your Eyes: Beautiful Recipes to Garnish, Share, and Savor.

    It has been revealed that “In 2027, I’d love to finally visit Peru and see Machu Picchu. South America is completely newly introduced territory for me, and the landscapes, craftsmanship, and food are all calling. I’m imagining local guides, time in the Sacred Valley, and plenty of exploring. I’d also love to go home to Mauritius, but this time be a tourist. A beautiful hotel, all the food I miss, and time to enjoy the island and its lovely hospitality. Usually, my visits revolve around family and catching up. In 2027, for once, I’d like my biggest responsibility to be deciding what to have for lunch.” —Nashmita Rajiah, interior designer.

    “I’m perpetually scouting [destinations] for In Hand’s newsletter and group trips by exploring culturally rich regions through the lens of traditional craft. I'm looking forward to an upcoming trip to the Atlas Mountains to visit the female Amazigh weavers in their homes, and learning about the by-hand process of weaving Berber rugs at the source rather than the point of sale, focusing on the culture and traditions around this generation-to-generation craft. I’m staying at Kasbah du Toubkal in Imlil, a small mountain town grounded in real Amazigh village life. It’s a trip I’ve wanted to take for years. ” —Meghan McEwen, writer and founder of group trip planner In Hand.

    Recent findings suggest that “What I look forward to most is traveling with friends and family. Mornings in the sea, a simple lunch in the hot sun. Afternoons are for slow wandering, and at night we'll cook massive meals from our market finds. In 2027, my family is heading to Sicily for two weeks in shoulder season, before the [summer] tourist wave. The first half we'll explore the main island, from the salt flats of Trapani to the bone white cliffs of Scala dei Turchi on the south coast. Then Favignana in the Egadi Islands, off Sicily's west coast, will hopefully be home for a week or so. The water is crystal blue, the coves are plentiful, and you can bike around the entire island easily. Tuna is still king there, though the old canning factory has long since closed. I'm dreaming of spaghetti with bottarga. At the moment I have my eyes on Villa Zu Nillu from The Thinking Traveller, perched above its own labyrinthine Roman stone quarry, into which a beautiful pool and a Mediterranean garden have been set. And I will document it all.” —Andrea Gentl, photographer and author of Cooking with Mushrooms.

    Sources indicate that “After last summer’s European heatwave, we’re planning a cooler 2027 Finnish escape with my decorative arts grad school friend and her family. We always mix design with fun for the kids, so we’ll visit Helsinki’s Aalto House, the design district, and Hvitträsk museum before renting a lakeside mökki for swimming, hiking, and archipelago adventures. I want to experience the “midnight sun,” but I might regret it if the kids never sleep. Truthfully, I’m more of a lazy reptile than an outdoor adventurer, so afterward, our family of four will retreat to a less popular Italian beach for pasta, sunshine, and absolutely no obligation to do anything adventurous at all.” —Ajiri Aki, author of JOIE: A Parisian’s Guide to Celebrating The Good Life and The Joie Journal.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • With snow already falling in the Rockies and a strong El Niño weather pattern expected to benefit certain US mountain regions, skiers and riders are already dusting off their gear and booking their winter trips.
    • Of course, skiing and snowboarding aren’t typically budget-friendly sports.
    • But in recent years, the industry has moved away from one-day lift tickets in favor of multi-mountain ski passes with heavily discounted rates and additional perks, like Epic’s “Pay Over Time” or Ikon’s deals on friends and family tickets.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    With snow already falling in the Rockies and a strong El Niño weather pattern expected to benefit certain US mountain regions, skiers and riders are already dusting off their gear and booking their winter trips.

    Of course, skiing and snowboarding aren’t typically budget-friendly sports. Once you factor in meals, lodging, and transportation in addition to a lift ticket (which costs well over $300 per day at several US resorts), it’s almost worth taking out a loan to pay for a one-week family ski trip.

    But in recent years, the industry has moved away from one-day lift tickets in favor of multi-mountain ski passes with heavily discounted rates and additional perks, like Epic’s “Pay Over Time” or Ikon’s deals on friends and family tickets.

    The dreamy Significant Bear Resort is included on Ikon Pass.

    Sources indicate that "For those who ski or ride more than six to eight days a season, multi-mountain passes have reshaped the [ski] resort industry,” notes Olivia Rowan, publisher of trade magazine Ski Area Management. “The multi-mountain pass opened up fresh possibilities for snow sports travel and tourism beyond your home hill. They're a great deal for an in-the-know skier or rider.”.

    Before choosing a pass, determine your skiing goals for the season. If you’re looking to check out a handful of newly introduced resorts for a day or two each, the Indy Pass might be your best option. But if you’re hoping to spend a week at a more popular resort like Park City, the Epic or Ikon passes are the way to go. To figure out which pass is best for you and your travel plans, here's a breakdown of the major players.

    Best for: Individuals and families who want unlimited access to some of the world's largest and most popular ski areas.

    When the Vail-owned Epic Pass debuted in 2008, it was the first of its kind and set the stage for the multi-mountain passes that followed in the coming years. Today, it remains one of the biggest players in the industry, offering access to over 90 resorts in North America, Europe, Japan, and Australia.

    Pricing: The standard Epic Pass, which offers unlimited access to all its resorts, costs $1,169. But if you don’t proposal to ski during holiday weeks and weekends, consider the Epic Local Pass, which excludes peak dates at certain resorts. Epic also offers a customizable pass that lets skiers choose up to 7 days across different resort tiers. The cheapest option, at $337, gives skiers 7 days at 22 resorts in the Midwest, Northeast, and Mid-Atlantic.

    Epic Pass offers access to over 90 resorts in North America, Europe, Japan, and Australia.

    Vail, Colorado, one of the most popular mountains included with Epic Pass.

    Where to visit with the Epic Pass:.

    Traveler-approved ski resorts near Epic Pass mountains:.

    Best for: Skiers and riders who want to check out several uncrowded, under-the-radar ski resorts.

    Industry observers note that the Indy Pass, which is the antithesis of larger passes like Epic and Ikon, offers two days of skiing at each of its over 300 partner resorts across four continents. The pass partners with smaller, independently owned resorts that are typically uncrowded and have deeply rooted local vibes. This season, Indy is rolling out an upgrade that lets passholders ski up to five days at 13 resorts, starting at $199. The pass sells out quickly and is already off sale for the 2026-27 ski season, but now is the time to get on the waiting list for next season (sales sometimes reopen mid-season, too).

    Pricing: The Indy+ Pass, which doesn’t have blackout dates, costs $469 for adults and $299 for kids 12 and under.

    Jay Peak mountain resort in Vermont, which saw record snowfall last winter.

    Where to visit with the Indy Pass:.

    Traveler-approved ski resorts near Indy Pass mountains:.

    Best for: Skiers who live near one of Ikon’s premier destinations, or families with children who want to take advantage of Ikon’s discounted kids passes.

    Sources indicate that like the Epic Pass, the Ikon Pass offers unlimited access to some of the world’s most popular ski resorts. The pass includes access to over 70 resorts across 13 countries, including some bigger US destinations like Jackson Hole, Deer Valley, and Aspen Snowmass.

    According to recent reports, pricing: Like Epic, Ikon offers tiered passes, with its unlimited pass starting at $1,529 (or $1,129 for young adults ages 13-22 and $499 for children ages 5-12). The base pass, which has some blackout dates, starts at $1,099 for adults over 23. Skiers and riders who want to dip their toes into the sport or who may not have time to get out much during the season should consider a personalized pass that allows two, three, or four days at partner resorts.

    Fresh powder at Substantial Bear Mountain Resort, a gem of a mountain on the Ikon Pass.

    Where to visit with the Ikon Pass:.

    Traveler-approved ski resorts near Ikon Pass mountains:.

    Best for: East Coast skiers and riders who mostly plan on skiing in the Mid-Atlantic, Northeast, or eastern Canada, or individuals looking to supplement another multi-mountain pass; It includes two mountains in Colorado and Wyoming, but they are on the smaller side.

    Upcoming for the 2026-27 ski season, the Snow Pass is the newest player in the game. Like Indy, the Snow Pass offers two days at each partner resort, but so far it has only 14 resorts to choose from, most of which are in the Northeast. You can buy additional days for 30% off the retail price. Snow Pass offers an alternate three-day pass—Snow Triple Play—that includes three days total at 23 partner resorts.

    Pricing: The Snow Pass costs $379.99, and the Snow Triple Play costs $189.99.

    Whiteface Mountain Ski Resort is a haven of varied terrain for skiers and snowboarders alike.

    Where to visit with the Snow Pass:.

    Traveler-approved ski resorts near Snow Pass mountains:.

    Best for: Skiers and riders who want to check some major-name resorts off their list but aren’t looking to ski for an extended period at one ski area, or those looking to supplement another multi-mountain or season pass.

    The Mountain Collective Pass offers passholders two days each at its 27 resorts in the US, Canada, Japan, Europe, South America, Australia, and Latest Zealand. It’s a slightly more affordable alternative to the Epic and Ikon, yet it still gives skiers access to significant-name resorts like Jackson Hole and Big Sky.

    It has been revealed that pricing: The Mountain Collective Pass goes for $729 for adults, $594 for teens, and $304 for kids 6-12. Skiers and riders who want to ski more than their allotted 2 days at a specific resort can purchase day tickets at half off.

    A sprawling mountain view at Jackson Hole, included on the Mountain Collective pass.

    #30634. Latest Update: Delta Air Lines Cuts JFK–Dulles Route After More Than 30 Years

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (796 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Liveandletsfly ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Delta Air Lines Cuts JFK–Dulles Route After More Than 30 Years

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (796 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, delta Air Lines will end nonstop service between Washington Dulles and New York JFK in February, leaving the two airports without a direct link.
    • Delta will operate its final flight between Washington Dulles (IAD) and Upcoming York Kennedy (JFK) on February 10, 2027.
    • But passengers who specifically want to connect at JFK on Delta or its partners will lose an option.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, delta Air Lines will end nonstop service between Washington Dulles and New York JFK in February, leaving the two airports without a direct link. The cut removes another connection to Delta’s JFK hub and follows similar exits by United and JetBlue.

    Delta will operate its final flight between Washington Dulles (IAD) and Upcoming York Kennedy (JFK) on February 10, 2027. The move eliminates the only nonstop link between the two airports (JetBlue cut the route in 2019 and United in 2014). Delta is not leaving Dulles, nor will this route cut eliminate flights between Dulles and the New York metropolitan area. United serves Newark and LaGuardia from its Washington hub.

    But passengers who specifically want to connect at JFK on Delta or its partners will lose an option.

    This route has run for over 30 years, so the route cut is certainly newsworthy. Without seeing Delta’s route economics, I’m not going to speculate how much money this service made or lost. But I struggle to see a large number of passengers who need this particular connection and cannot reasonably be accommodated elsewhere. I’m frankly surprised Delta operated a route like this for so long, which sounds like the sort of slot-squatting United does by scheulding so many flights between Washington National and Newark.

    Sources indicate that the case for this route has always been onward connections at JFK, particularly to international flights. But even there, Delta has alternatives. Washington-area passengers can begin at Reagan National (DCA), while travelers who prefer Dulles can connect through another Delta hub, such as Atlanta or Detroit, depending on their destination. I cannot imagine that there is so connecting traffic from Northern Virginia and the broader Washington area that Delta cannot handle it through DCA or another hub.

    While I’m sure there will be “regulars” who are greatly inconvenienced by this route cut, that’s no justification to keep any route going and we do know the load factor was lower on this route than its network average.

    This brought back memories of my coverage of United ending JFK–Dulles service in October 2014.

    “Two-thirds of traffic on the route is connecting traffic that does not generate sufficient yields.”.

    Recent findings suggest that united’s circumstances were somewhat similar. Dulles was its hub, while JFK had become a small station focused on flights to Los Angeles and San Francisco. Today, Delta operates a substantial hub at JFK, but it only flies to its hubs, now less JFK, from IAD.

    In both cases the underlying question is similar: does the connecting revenue justify using an aircraft and scarce airport access on a short route when passengers have other ways to reach the network?

    Sources indicate that united decided it did not. Delta is now removing the same airport pair from its schedule.

    More than 12 years later, I still find United’s explanation brutally honest as to why it cut that route (and eventually pulled out of JFK altogether).

    I have written about Delta becoming more selective at JFK, including cuts to domestic feeder routes and international destinations. With air traffic control congestion and slot restrictions still in place, it makes sense to me that Delta would want to funnel less travel through JFK and more throughout other hubs: the focus must be on local traffic or at least costal traffic that can command a higher premium.

    Meanwhile, United is preparing to return to JFK through its partnership with JetBlue. Does this create an opening for United to restore Dulles service? Perhaps, but I would think it would be difficult to work now just like it was then and has been for Delta. United already has extensive Washington–New York connectivity through Newark, and its initial JFK access will be limited. Each available slot will have more compelling uses via transcon traffic.

    I do not think the disappearance of Delta from this route will make starting that route attractive to United, especially since United previously abandoned it.

    Delta will end JFK–Dulles flights after February 10, 2027, removing a useful option for some Washington-area passengers connecting through Kennedy. Even so, the decision makes sense to me. Delta can accommodate much of that traffic through Reagan National or other hubs, and local Washington–Newly introduced York travelers have several alternatives…so no, this isn’t a sign that Delta is continuing to lose ground in New York.

    United cut this route in 2014 because connecting traffic did not produce sufficient revenue. Delta has not publicly supplied the same explanation, but the commercial question remains much the same. A “useful connection” for many passengers does not necessarily mean a profitable or smart one for the airline.

    #30633. Independents decide the election, again!

    📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1151 w)

    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Independents decide the election, again!

    📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1151 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Once more, independents were the decisive factor in what amounts to the Republicans’ midterm disaster that was both broad and deep.
    • “We hired you to fix the Biden economy and you failed.” Pretty simple.
    • Industry observers note that according to the exit polls, Democrats won independents by an astonishing 22 points.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Once more, independents were the decisive factor in what amounts to the Republicans’ midterm disaster that was both broad and deep. No one who reads this column should have been surprised that this growing segment of the electorate became the equivalent of the “deciders-in-chief” who used their vote to send a tough message to the president and his party.

    “We hired you to fix the Biden economy and you failed.” Pretty simple.

    Industry observers note that according to the exit polls, Democrats won independents by an astonishing 22 points. If this holds, it will be the largest margin in the history of exit polling, beating the Republican margin in 2010 of 19 points. For Republicans, this is the fifth consecutive election losing independents.

    It was the size of the GOP defeat with independents that put the number of states and congressional districts into play, districts that President Donald Trump won in 2024, many by double digits.

    Independents made up 33 percent of the electorate; Democrats were at 35 percent and Republicans at 32 percent. This is the second consecutive election where independents were a larger part of the electorate than one of the major parties. It also shows that while independents may not have been enthused about voting, they highlighted up.

    Sources indicate that looking at the 13 battleground Senate races, which now include Mississippi, Democrats won independents in all of them by double digits, and 10 of them by 20 points or more. The independent vote allowed Democrats to overwhelm significant Republican Party ID advantages in many red states and districts.

    For example, in Kansas (exit poll not final), Republicans had a 17-point party advantage, but lost independents by 33. Incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall went down with a 5-point loss. In South Carolina, Republicans had a 14-point party advantage, but lost independents by 31 points. A liberal activist Democrat beat a neophyte Republican candidate, appointed Sen. Darline Graham, by 4 points.

    According to recent reports, despite Texas Republicans’ 5-point party ID advantage, Ken Paxton lost independents by 31 points and lost the Senate race by a huge 12 points. It goes without saying that voters in Texas shocked Republicans by not only rejecting the president’s primary choice for Senate, but taking down all Republicans in statewide races.

    In a recent development, overall, Republicans lost six states with key Senate races where Trump won by double digits in 2024, with Mississippi being a potential seventh. In the House (with 7 races yet to be called at the time of this writing), Democrats have won 56 congressional districts that Trump carried in 2024, along with carrying all 201 districts that Harris won.

    It has been revealed that clearly, Republican operatives, consultants and the media missed the boat when it came to evaluating the viability of House races. Using the 2024 Trump-Harris race results to assess the safety or vulnerability of a particular seat proved to be the wrong context.

    Industry observers note that in the spring, I was beginning to see some danger signals in our polling and in public surveys that raised questions for me about just how many House seats were actually in play, fearing perhaps far more than anyone was predicting. By early summer, I decided to undertake a different analysis on the state of current races using the 2020 Trump-Biden results by congressional district. The research found a much larger number of GOP seats could be vulnerable. In the end, the analysis proved to be right. Democrats won all of the 220 districts that Biden carried, and at least 37 seats that Trump won.

    According to recent reports, according to the exit polls, the independent vote, not surprisingly, was largely driven by the economy, their top problem concern. Much to the detriment of Trump and the Republicans, 80 percent of independents thought the economy was not good/poor, versus 20 percent who thought the economy was excellent/good. In terms of inflation, 82 percent stated it had been a severe or moderate hardship for them, and 89 percent said the cost of living was a crucial or major factor in how they voted for Congress.

    The president and his party got the blame. Looking at specific policies, 71 percent of independents thought that Trump’s tariff policies had hurt the national economy, and more broadly, 72 percent mentioned his policies had worsened economic conditions in the country. As a result, Trump’s overall job approval among these voters was 29 percent approve with 71 disapproving; 59 percent strongly disapproving. These extraordinarily bad numbers topped even Biden’s worst job approval numbers.

    Recent findings suggest that trump’s decision to ask voters to “pretend I’m on the ballot,” was, in retrospect, a strategic miscalculation. It was a mistake to tell voters that the economy was in great shape when it was clear the majority of people were very unhappy when it came to inflation — the rising cost of gas and groceries.

    A little empathy on economic challenges and a lot better explanation of why the Iran conflict was crucial to national security and worth the economic sacrifice would have gone a long way to minimizing the size of the GOP defeat.

    Sources indicate that neither happened, and Republicans were overwhelmed by a blue tsunami almost nobody saw coming. Still, despite the size of the Democrats’ win, they would be wrong to see this as an ideological mandate of any sort. The exit polls highlighted that the electorate remains center-right. Moderates are the largest component at 41 percent, but conservatives still outnumber liberals by a 33-26 margin.

    Independents have a negative view of both parties. Their view of Republicans is 32 percent favorable and 68 percent unfavorable. However, Democrats are not far behind, at 42 percent favorable and 58 percent unfavorable.

    In a recent development, at a policy level when independents were asked which party was better able to handle the economy, 41 percent said the Democratic Party, 28 percent said the Republican Party, and 30 percent said neither. Both parties are well short of a majority. This reflects the fact that the electorate still negatively remembers the Biden economy, but also believes that Republicans didn’t fix it as they promised two years ago.

    According to recent reports, democrats would be wise to moderate and not continue down the increasingly extreme progressive path. Republicans and the president need to take a hard look at their own failings and understand that when it comes to voters, especially independents, all the money in the world is no substitute for good candidates with real solutions.

    Recent findings suggest that david Winston is the president of The Winston Group and a longtime adviser to congressional Republicans. He previously served as the director of planning for Speaker Newt Gingrich. He advises Fortune 100 companies, foundations and nonprofit organizations on strategic planning and public policy issues, as well as serving as an election analyst for CBS News.

Patagonia also offers two-day delivery and next-day delivery for an added fee if you need a quicker turnaround on last-minute road trip, camping, backpacking, or hiking gear.

    White House warns Democrats against aggressive oversight

    📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (631 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Trump administration signaled it would respond aggressively to a Democratic-led Congress with a letter this week threatening to prosecute lawmakers for oversight efforts.
    • The letter from White House Counsel Will Scharf sent Monday to House Oversight and Government Reform ranking member Robert Garcia, D-Calif., argued that members of Congress have limited authority to conduct oversight of a presidential administration and that some of the threats to glitch subpoenas “may cross the line into blatant criminality.”.
    • Recent findings suggest that the letter, obtained from a White House official, marks the latest escalation from the Trump administration ahead of Democrats taking control of both chambers of Congress next year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Trump administration signaled it would respond aggressively to a Democratic-led Congress with a letter this week threatening to prosecute lawmakers for oversight efforts.

    The letter from White House Counsel Will Scharf sent Monday to House Oversight and Government Reform ranking member Robert Garcia, D-Calif., argued that members of Congress have limited authority to conduct oversight of a presidential administration and that some of the threats to glitch subpoenas “may cross the line into blatant criminality.”.

    Recent findings suggest that the letter, obtained from a White House official, marks the latest escalation from the Trump administration ahead of Democrats taking control of both chambers of Congress next year. It also dovetails with years of Trump’s threats to prosecute his critics.

    “We are monitoring the abusive and capricious threats that are now proliferating from Democrat legislators who seek to abuse the legislative process to intimidate and to interfere with the lawful functioning of government,” the letter says.

    Garcia, the likely committee chair next Congress, pushed back on the threat in a statement Wednesday, accusing the administration of having “something to hide” and that Congress has wide authority to investigate the executive branch.

    “The American people voted overwhelmingly for us to pass laws to root out corruption and abuse," Garcia said. "The Trump Administration continues to weaponize the government with threats of unconstitutional attacks on Congress. We are a co-equal branch of government and will not be deterred by baseless threats from a weaponized DOJ or from the President’s lawyers.”.

    The letter came after Attorney General Todd Blanche previously refused to rule out criminal charges against members of Congress in response to investigations.

    "It depends on what the crime is and what they have done,” Blanche told CNN over the weekend.

    Last week, President Donald Trump himself stated that threats of investigations and impeachment were “extortion at the highest level” and called for the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act, immediately!”.

    He also singled out Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., calling for her to be imprisoned. The administration previously unsuccessfully attempted to indict Slotkin and other Democrats over a video she published calling for soldiers to disobey illegal orders.

    According to recent reports, and Trump last year publicly called for longtime critic Sen. Adam B. Schiff, D-Calif., to face unspecified charges in a post on Truth Social addressed to then-Attorney General Pam Bondi that also called for the prosecution of former FBI Director James Comey and New York Attorney General Letitia James. Both have faced criminal charges, pleaded not guilty and fought them in court as political attacks.

    According to recent reports, garcia and other Democrats have signaled they intend to pursue oversight aggressively in the newly introduced Congress. After Democrats won the House majority last week, Garcia put out an all-caps statement urging administration officials to “LAWYER UP” ahead of the new year.

    Garcia, as well as other likely incoming chairs such as House Judiciary ranking member Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md.; Homeland Security ranking member Rep. Bennie Thompson, D-Miss.; and Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., have hinted at broad inquiries ranging from the handling of files related to deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein to immigration enforcement and more.

    Raskin told reporters last week that he thought Democratic oversight efforts could dovetail with the party’s broader effort to address affordability issues, including by addressing the Iran war, allegations of corruption within the Trump administration and more.

    “We're going to get all the information that we need in order to restore the rule of law in American constitutional democracy,” Raskin remarked.

    The letter also echoes a previous fight the administration pitched with the House in the first Trump administration, where officials resisted in court allowing former White House Counsel Don McGahn to testify to the House Judiciary Committee for years.

    Industry News: Aer Lingus Unveils Business Class Suites With Doors And Its First Premium Economy Cabin On A330s

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (845 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Aer Lingus has declared a cabin overhaul for 10 Airbus A330 aircraft, with the first refurbished jet scheduled to enter service on October 1, 2027.
    • This is an A330-only project for now: there will be no corresponding cabin overhaul for the Airbus A321LR or A321XLR.
    • According to recent reports, the refurbished aircraft will feature 28 Collins Elevation business class suites in a 1-2-1 layout.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Aer Lingus has declared a cabin overhaul for 10 Airbus A330 aircraft, with the first refurbished jet scheduled to enter service on October 1, 2027. The initial route will be Dublin–Fresh York JFK, on select EI104/EI105 services. Additional North American routes will follow as more aircraft are refurbished.

    This is an A330-only project for now: there will be no corresponding cabin overhaul for the Airbus A321LR or A321XLR.

    According to recent reports, the refurbished aircraft will feature 28 Collins Elevation business class suites in a 1-2-1 layout. Every passenger will have direct aisle access and a closing door, with each seat converting into a 78-inch flat bed. Improved bedding and amenity kits are also planned.

    The renderings look attractive to me. Green upholstery and lighter finishes give the cabin an Irish identity and a premium feel (hello Singapore Airlines). More importantly, the layout addresses a weakness I encountered on my Aer Lingus A330-200 flight from Dublin to Los Angeles. I had a window seat with a passenger beside me and no direct aisle access. Storage was limited too.

    According to recent reports, I slept well, but the seat was behind what many competitors offered. The lovely crew helped redeem that flight, though warm service should complement a competitive seat rather than compensate for one. Doors are fine, but giving every passenger access to the aisle is the more consequential improvement.

    Aer Lingus also intends refreshed dining and a self-service business class snack and refreshment bar, much like SAS offers its on its A330 aircraft:.

    The latest premium economy cabin will have four rows of Recaro R4 seats:.

    Passengers will receive an upgraded three-course meal, complimentary drinks, bedding, an amenity kit, and noise-reducing headphones. It’s a hardly a unique or transformative hard product compared to its peers, but it’s an increasingly important middle way providing a noticeably more comfortable seat at a price that makes sense relative to economy and business class.

    This fills an obvious gap for Aer Lingus. Someone who wants more room than economy offers but cannot justify a business class fare right now has limited options within the airline’s own cabin lineup. A genuine premium economy product gives that passenger another reason to stay with Aer Lingus.

    In a recent development, economy will retain the A330’s appealing 2-4-2 layout, with new seats and adjustable headrests. A self-service snack station is coming to this cabin too.

    Industry observers note that if I fly economy class, I prefer the A330 or 767. Two seats together by the window remain a compelling reason to choose an A330 when traveling as a couple, especially compared with being part of a block of three on most other widebody aircraft.

    Aer Lingus promises more personal space, but we will wait for the final seat pitch and total economy seat count before drawing conclusions about legroom. A redesigned seatback can improve knee clearance without increasing the distance between rows, but padding is also essential.

    The snack station is a nice touch.

    The refurbished A330s will receive Panasonic Astrova entertainment systems, with 4K screens, Bluetooth headphone pairing, and USB-C charging.

    Free Starlink Wi-Fi will also be available, though Aer Lingus states that service is already offered across its transatlantic routes. Passengers do not need to wait for the fresh cabins to benefit from it. My previous A330 flight featured an entertainment system with missing graphics and internet that was slow but stable. Working screens and fast connectivity would improve the experience considerably.

    Sources indicate that for a daytime transatlantic flight, I place enormous value on reliable internet. A better seat may help me sleep on the overnight journey to Dublin, but Starlink makes the flight home a far more useful part of my day.

    The first aircraft is still almost a year away, and the announcement does not provide a completion date for all 10 retrofits.

    An October 1 launch on select JFK flights should not be confused with every Aer Lingus A330 having the latest cabins from that date, even to JFK. During the transition, you’ll be able to tell which aircraft have the new business class because that aircraft will also be selling premium economy seats.

    I hope Aer Lingus makes the differences clear during booking and handles aircraft substitutions sensibly….

    Aer Lingus is giving 10 A330s fresh business class suites, adding premium economy, and refreshing economy class, with the first aircraft scheduled to debut between Dublin and New York JFK in October 2027.

    It has been revealed that my last longhaul flight on Aer Lingus left me impressed by the crew but disappointed by parts of the onboard product. This overhaul addresses the seat and technology shortcomings that made me reluctant to seek out the airline. I look forward to trying it. Aer Lingus already showed me how pleasant its service can be. Pair that with a competitive seat and better catering, and I might go out of my way to book it again.
